criteria: For native-only, bridge-only, both-present, neither-present, reinstall, resume, and repeated-onboarding Codex fixtures, each taskPlane hook event produces exactly one trace row or side effect, configuration is idempotent, and unrelated hooks remain unchanged.

For personal or managed and trusted or untrusted host fixtures, onboarding separately reports install, trust, managed-policy, loaded-session, and effective-path state; no file-presence false green, trust bypass instruction, or managed-setting overwrite is allowed.

The same frozen review and evaluate payload through Claude workflow and Task or Codex transport yields byte-identical canonical ReviewKernel artifacts and equivalent collection; wrong, missing, duplicate, copied, stale, or unobserved slot evidence fails identically.

Workflow resume reuses a result only when target, context, view, lease, schema, slot, producer, and canonical revision match; mismatch receives a bounded retry or named failure and no workflow agent can gate, approve, or advance state.

Every live skill, loop evaluator, and leased reviewer declares and validates one versioned output schema before record, collection, or gate; native structured output is used when supported and an exact governed host-observed JSON file is validated otherwise, while prose or schema-invalid output cannot pass.

Supported, unsupported, unknown, contradictory, and corrupt capability fixtures select native schema or governed file fallback deterministically, record source and reason, preserve write scope and evidence requirements, and never convert unavailable evidence to pass or zero.

A submission-required contract with missing, wrong-slot, wrong-workspace, corrupt, or absent submission blocks Stop or SubagentStop with contract, slot, missing artifact, and safe recovery details while leaving the contract active and loop state unchanged.

Valid submitted work, sibling slots, canonical review results, and submission records remain byte-identical through repeated Stop and SubagentStop; stop handling never gates or clears them, and standalone or no-submission-required contracts retain their documented lifecycle.

Claude Task and workflow plus Codex native dispatch fixtures prove cheap, standard, and deep selections reach the actual child invocation and host receipt whenever supported, including model aliases and supported effort values.

Cross-provider ids, unsupported effort, old or corrupt capability, strict, warn, and default fixtures send no foreign or unsupported argument; fallback is explicit, and strict mode blocks before work when a required explicit route cannot be honored.

Evaluation records validate a versioned lifecycle schema containing host capability source, transport, schema fallback, task or slot or lease, planned and observed routing, attempts, duration, terminal and validation status, telemetry availability, and bounded redacted diagnostics.

Claude and Codex usage goldens, nested usage, duplicate messages, torn JSONL, absent fields, and corrupt values reconcile uncached input, cached input, cache creation, output, raw total, and effective tokens exactly without double counting; missing telemetry is unavailable with reason.

Claude and Codex both deliver the exact engine-authored canonical review dashboard inline where the host supports it, with the dependency graph merged into that dashboard as one human-facing entity; no host-authored substitute is accepted, while the dashboard and standalone graph remain durable content-addressed artifacts by reference.
Standalone review always stops at one explicit human approve/request-changes gate; remote source or storage approval is never inferred or skipped.

Review preflight explicitly offers optional dynamic validation and optional inline functionality rendering; permissions, dependency installs, process execution, and browser access are structured user approval actions, and the review records selected, declined, unavailable, and executed evidence; static-only review remains possible and is labeled.

Clean lens results include compact source-anchored checked evidence and render notes or observations; findings are semantically deduplicated without erasing lens, slot, source, or revision provenance.

The canonical dashboard records engine/version, routing-policy, graph, and routing-decision fingerprints and contains workflow/waves, findings/notes, the merged dependency graph, dynamic-validation/render evidence, and the single approve/request-changes gate.

The complete suite passes on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, macOS, and Windows, and existing green hooks, package or manifest, docs, release-history, and dispatch-parity jobs stay green with no removed, skipped, xfailed, loosened, or de-gated test.

Claude/Codex PR-review parity evals compare the complete routing dispositions and semantic finding clusters rather than exact wording or raw finding count, while requiring identical canonical dashboard, graph, provenance, gate, and fingerprint identities.

Documentation presents one engine-authored review dashboard—not separate competing graph and report surfaces—with durable artifact references, optional dynamic validation/rendering approvals, explicit static-only labeling, and one human approve/request-changes gate on both hosts.

tasks.tests: python3 -m pytest -q taskplane/tests/test_review_preflight.py taskplane/tests/test_review_target.py taskplane/tests/test_review_evidence.py taskplane/tests/test_loop.py
criteria: Before Review, Build, Design, or governed delivery selects its process, the engine inventories available DoR artifacts and records admitted, rejected, missing, and conflicting candidates with fingerprints and precedence evidence.

For a pull request, commit subjects and bodies, changed changelog or release-note entries, linked requirement/spec files, and repository-local contribution/test instructions are considered specification candidates and admitted into the canonical context when applicable.

A PR with usable commit or changelog specification does not fall back to an inferred generic goal; a conflict between artifacts and the prompt pauses at DoR with the exact conflict instead of silently selecting a flow.

Recording failed dynamic validation without an execution receipt persists safely, marks side effects as started, remains dynamic rather than static-only, and creates a high-severity canonical finding.

The validation sandbox is an independent clone pinned to the reviewed HEAD plus the exact reviewed tracked patch and eligible untracked inputs; Taskplane evidence, dependencies, build outputs, symlinks, and escaping paths are excluded or refused.

Validation-only repair changes neither the original checkout nor its verdict identity, cannot push through its configured remote or hook, and records successful execution as conditional sandbox evidence while preserving the original failure finding.
Focused review and artifact-DoR suites pass, generated CLI documentation is current, and the complete suite is run once with no skips, xfails, weakened assertions, or de-gating.
